name: Prone leg raise
movement: one straight leg lifted a hand's width off the floor and lowered

phone.placement: Lay the phone on its side on the floor, two or three metres away, side on to where you will be.

words.hint: Lying face down, one straight leg lifted a little off the floor.
words.start: Lay the phone on its side on the floor. Lie face down side on to it, legs straight, forehead on your hands.
words.position: Lie face down, side on to the phone, legs straight, forehead resting on your hands, hips pressed into the floor.
words.top: One straight leg lifted a hand's width off the floor — five to twelve degrees at the hip — hips still on the floor, toes pointed back, held a second.
howto: Lie face down with your forehead on your hands and both legs straight.
Tighten the buttock and lift one straight leg a hand's width off the floor — about six inches. Both hip bones stay on the floor.
Hold for the count without arching the lower back or lifting the chest.
Lower slowly. The rep counts when the foot is back down.
words.cannot: The pelvis rolling and the lower back muscles taking over: it sees the lift, the knee and the shoulders coming up. Lift from the buttock, not the back.
words.about: Prone leg raise — lying face down side on: the lift, as the angle at the hip between shoulder and ankle read as the change from the rest position, which the coach follows slowly while the leg is near it, so one person's 172 at rest and another's 180 both count as 0 and a rest that settles moves with it; a rep is under way past 7° of lift and counts when the leg is back within 3° of rest; at the top a lift of 5–25° (a hand's width is 5–12°); the knee at least 155° so the leg stays straight; the shoulders no more than 12° above the hips, which is the back arching; the hip no more than 6° above the shoulder (the hip coming off the floor); at the top the toes pointed back (the foot angle at the heel at least 100°) and the foot's length as the camera sees it at least 70% of the most it has been — a leg swinging toward or away from the camera foreshortens it. Hold a second at the top (the clock starts 0.3 s after the leg is up), lower slowly, and the rep counts when the foot is down. Feet to shoulders must be in the picture.
words.lost: Lie face down side on to the camera, feet to shoulders in the picture
words.early: Hold it at the top next time
words.safety: This is a small lift. Stop if the lower back pinches; lift less high next time.
words.easier: A smaller lift; a pillow under the hips.
words.harder: A longer hold; an ankle weight.
words.mistakes: Lifting the hip off the floor to get height; arching the back; bending the knee; pulling the toes up; swinging the leg out to the side.

measurements.label: lift from rest

settings.label: Lift at the top, most (degrees from rest)
Lift at the top, least (degrees from rest)

measurements.why: The leg against the trunk, as the change from the rest position: 0 lying as the person lies, -7 a hand's width up (ten centimetres at the foot of an eighty-five centimetre leg is seven degrees at the hip). The rest reference follows the reading slowly and only while the leg is near it, because the angle at rest is 170-176 for one person and 180 for another, wanders a few degrees with the model, and settles as the set goes on. A hand's width is -5 to -12; past -25 the back is arching or the leg is far too high. Also the progress measurement.

measurements.label: knee straight

settings.label: Knee angle, at least (180 is straight)

measurements.why: The knee kept straight: 180 is locked out, though lying face down the model reads a straight knee at 160-168. Below the band it is bending.

measurements.label: shoulders above hips

settings.label: Shoulders above the hips, at most

measurements.why: The hip-to-shoulder line off level: the shoulders coming up is the chest lifting and the back arching to make height.

measurements.label: hip above the shoulder

settings.label: Hip above the shoulder, at most (degrees)

measurements.why: The shoulder-to-hip line off level, + with the hip the higher: the hip coming up off the floor to help the lift. Judged through the rep.

measurements.label: toe, heel, knee

settings.label: Foot angle, at least (180 is toes straight back)

measurements.why: The foot against the shin at the heel: toes pointed straight back reads 150 or more, toes pulled up toward the shin 90 or so. Judged through the rep.

measurements.label: foot length, % of the most seen

settings.label: Foot length, % of the most seen, at least

measurements.why: The heel-to-toe length as the camera sees it, against the longest it has been in the set: a leg lifted in line with the body keeps the foot side on, the same length; a leg swinging toward or away from the camera foreshortens it. Under 85% it has gone diagonal. Judged through the rep.

prompt.text: Lift one leg — just a little

faults.label: Knee bending
faults.deep: Straighten the knee — lift the whole leg

faults.label: Back arching
faults.text: Chest down — lift from the hip, not the back
faults.deep: Lower the chest — the back is arching to make height

faults.label: Hip lifting
faults.text: Hips down on the floor — lift the leg, not the hip
faults.deep: Keep both hips flat on the floor — the hip is coming up

faults.label: Too high
faults.text: Not so high — a hand's width off the floor
faults.deep: Lower it — a small lift, hips on the floor

faults.label: Lift short
faults.deep: Higher — a hand's width off the floor

faults.label: Toes not straight
faults.text: Point the toes straight back, in line with the leg
faults.deep: Toes pointed — the foot is pulled up

faults.label: Leg going diagonal
faults.text: Lift the leg straight up, in line with your body — not out to the side
faults.deep: The leg is swinging across — straight up, in line with the body

settings.label: Lift that counts as under way (degrees from rest)
